response.sql: WITH exec_avg AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) as avg_remain FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ordersmark), benchmark1 AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) as b1 FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL), above_b1 AS (SELECT e.ordersmark, e.avg_remain, e.avg_remain - b.b1 as excess1 FROM exec_avg e, benchmark1 b WHERE e.avg_remain > b.b1), benchmark2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_remain) as b2 FROM above_b1), final_filter AS (SELECT a.ordersmark, a.avg_remain, a.excess1, a.avg_remain - b.b2 as excess2 FROM above_b1 a, benchmark2 b WHERE a.avg_remain > b.b2) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) as final_avg, AVG(excess1) as avg_excess_over_b1, AVG(excess2) as avg_excess_over_b2 FROM final_filter

assumptions.assumption: "Above" means strictly greater than (>), not ≥. This is the standard reading of "above" in comparative contexts.

"Ignoring missing values" applies to NULL remaincount when computing each order's average, not to NULL ordersmark. The schema allows ordersmark to be NULL, and the request explicitly states executions with no order reference (NULL ordersmark) count together as one order.
